# Copilot / AI Agent Instructions for `dbs-strona`

These notes are intended to get an AI coding agent productive in this Next.js + TypeScript site quickly.

1) Project overview
- Framework: Next.js (App Router) — source lives in the `app/` directory.
- Language: TypeScript (`tsconfig.json` strict mode enabled).
- UI: TailwindCSS utilities (see `app/globals.css`) and custom CSS variables (e.g. `--background`, `--foreground`).
- Entry points: `app/layout.tsx` (global layout, fonts, Header/Footer), `app/page.tsx` (home page).

2) Local developer commands
- Install and run dev server: `npm install` then `npm run dev` (runs `next dev`).
- Build for production: `npm run build` (runs `next build`).
- Start production server: `npm run start` (runs `next start`).
- Linting: `npm run lint` (runs `eslint`).

3) Key patterns & conventions (do not change without project-owner confirmation)
- App router: Add pages/routes under `app/<route>/page.tsx` (or nested folders) — `app/layout.tsx` wraps all pages.
- Component organization: Shared UI components live in `components/`. Imports use the path alias `@/` (maps to project root) — e.g. `import Header from "@/components/Header"`.
- Client vs Server components: `components/Header.tsx` is a client component (it starts with `'use client'` and uses React state). Preserve `'use client'` when a component uses hooks or browser APIs.
- Fonts: Fonts are added with `next/font/google` inside `layout.tsx` and exposed via CSS variables like `--font-montserrat`.
- Static assets: Put images/videos in `public/images/` and `public/videos/` and reference them like `/images/...` or `/videos/...` from JSX.

4) Project-specific CSS/Tailwind notes
- `app/globals.css` defines color and font variables (example: `--background`, `--main-accent`).
- The codebase uses custom utility-like classes consistently (e.g. `font-title`, `bg-(--background)`, `text-(--main-accent)`). Do not automatically refactor these; they are project-specific tokens and may be handled by the project's Tailwind configuration or conventions.

5) Routing & navigation conventions
- Header builds links from display names using a `slugify` helper (see `components/Header.tsx`) that maps Polish characters to ASCII. If you add routes, ensure they match the slug patterns used by `slugify` (or update the slugify function accordingly).
- When adding a new nav item, mirror the pattern used in `Header.tsx` menus: update `menus` or `rightLinks` arrays and create matching pages under `app/<slug>/page.tsx`.

6) Integration points and missing pieces to be aware of
- No API routes detected in the repo root; this is a static/static-with-SSR front-end app. If you add server/api routes, prefer `app/api/...` or Next.js route handlers.
- Deployments: README suggests Vercel. Expect standard Next.js deployment behaviour.

7) Linting, type-checking and formatting
- TypeScript: `tsconfig.json` is strict — prefer small, typed changes and keep `noEmit: true` intact.
- ESLint: Project uses Next.js ESLint presets via `eslint.config.mjs`. Run `npm run lint` to surface issues.

8) Small examples (copy/paste)
- Import a component using alias: `import Footer from "@/components/Footer";`
- Create a new route: `app/czym-jest-pakt/page.tsx` (match `slugify('CZYM JEST PAKT?')` => `czym-jest-pakt`).
- Reference a public asset: `<source src="/videos/leaves_background_loop.mp4" type="video/mp4" />` (file lives in `public/videos/`).

9) When changing UI or CSS
- Check `app/globals.css` for CSS variables names and reuse them (e.g. `--foreground`, `--main-accent`).
- Avoid bulk rewrites of Tailwind classes; follow existing class patterns and the project-specific token usage.

10) Conservative editing rules for AI
- Preserve `'use client'` at top of files that use React state or browser-only APIs.
- Preserve import alias `@/` usage and adjust `tsconfig.paths` only with human confirmation.
- When adding routes, ensure filenames and folder names match the slugs generated by `Header.tsx` slugify function (Polish char mapping).

If anything here is unclear or you'd like more detail (example: Tailwind config, Node version, or CI/deployment files), tell me which area to expand and I'll update the instructions.
